messages.content: You are BioGPT, an expert compiler architect. Translate the provided natural language biological protocol into valid, deterministic BioScript code for execution on a microfluidic biochip.

Source link: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3613134/pdf/nihms394155.pdf
Paper DOI: 10.1016/j.snb.2012.07.022

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Picoliter-Scale Electrowetting-on-Dielectric (EWD) Droplet Dispensing, Splitting, and Bead/Chemiluminescent Reaction Manipulation

REAGENTS USED:
  - DI Water (deionized water, test droplet fluid)
  - Paramagnetic Bead Solution (Invitrogen Dynabeads M-270 2.8 um streptavidin-functionalized paramagnetic beads)
  - Luciferase Buffer (1 ug/ul luciferase reagent solution)
  - Luciferin/ATP Substrate (400 ug/ml luciferin with 0.1 uM ATP)

STEPS:
1. Dispense an 18 pl DI water droplet from the reservoir on the 33 um electrode device (5 um gasket) at 17.1 Vrms.
2. Split the dispensed droplet into two daughter droplets by simultaneously activating two adjacent electrodes, then discard both resulting droplets after confirming successful splitting.
3. Dispense a 12 pl paramagnetic bead droplet from the reservoir on the 33 um electrode device with a 3 um gasket.
4. Split the bead droplet into two daughter droplets using the reservoir-electrode/third-channel-electrode splitting protocol; discard one daughter droplet.
5. Dispense a luciferase buffer droplet and a luciferin/ATP substrate droplet.
6. Merge the remaining bead droplet with the luciferase buffer droplet, then merge the resulting droplet with the luciferin/ATP substrate droplet to form the reaction droplet.
7. Incubate the merged reaction droplet at 25C for 1 minute.
8. Detect the chemiluminescent signal produced by the ATP-luciferin reaction using a cooled CCD/EMCCD camera sensor.
9. Discard the reaction droplet.

INTERPRETATION: Successful dispensing and splitting of picoliter-scale droplets (18 pl and 12 pl on 33 um electrodes; 5 pl on 21 um electrodes) at low actuation voltages (17.1-22 Vrms dispensing, 18.7 Vrms splitting) confirms the physical scaling and low-voltage operation of the multi-layer-insulator EWD platform. Successful dispensing of the 12 pl paramagnetic bead droplet at the same voltages used for DI water confirms that bead-containing droplets can be manipulated without additional actuation penalty. The paper notes that the resulting chemiluminescent signal from the ATP-luciferin reaction at this droplet scale was too low to be detected even with a cooled EMCCD camera, so the detection step models the intended assay workflow rather than a successful quantitative measurement obtained in this study.

module chemiluminescence

manifest DIWater
manifest ParamagneticBeadSolution
manifest LuciferaseBuffer
manifest LuciferinATPSubstrate

instructions:

water_droplet = dispense 18 units of DIWater
water_split = split water_droplet into 2
dispose water_split[0]
dispose water_split[1]

bead_droplet = dispense 12 units of ParamagneticBeadSolution
bead_split = split bead_droplet into 2
dispose bead_split[0]

enzyme = dispense 12 units of LuciferaseBuffer
substrate = dispense 12 units of LuciferinATPSubstrate

reaction = mix bead_split[1] with enzyme for 5s
reaction2 = mix reaction with substrate for 5s

heat reaction2 at 25c for 1m

light_signal = detect chemiluminescence on reaction2 for 30s

dispose reaction2

identity.protocol_name: Low Voltage Picoliter Droplet Manipulation Utilizing Electrowetting-on-Dielectric Platforms (Lin, Welch, and Fair, 2012)

source.title: Picoliter-Scale Electrowetting-on-Dielectric (EWD) Droplet Dispensing, Splitting, and Bead/Chemiluminescent Reaction Manipulation

ir.content:
main:
	water_droplet1[0] = dispense(DIWater)
	water_split1[2] = split(water_droplet1[0], 2)
	dispose(water_split1[0])
	dispose(water_split1[1])
	bead_droplet1[0] = dispense(ParamagneticBeadSolution)
	bead_split1[2] = split(bead_droplet1[0], 2)
	dispose(bead_split1[0])
	enzyme1[0] = dispense(LuciferaseBuffer)
	substrate1[0] = dispense(LuciferinATPSubstrate)
	reaction1[0] = mix(bead_split1[1], enzyme1[0]) @ 5.0SECOND
	reaction21[0] = mix(reaction1[0], substrate1[0]) @ 5.0SECOND
	heat(reaction21[0]) @ 25.0CELSIUS @ 60.0SECOND
	light_signal1[0] = detect(chemiluminescence, reaction21[0]) @ 30.0SECOND
	dispose(reaction21[0])
	NOP

chemical_evidence.source_quote: 10 nl DI water was then dispensed into the reservoirs by a pipette with the large reservoir electrode turned on.

Invitrogen Dynabeads M-270 2.8 um streptavidin-functionalized paramagnetic bead solution was dispensed into the reservoir, and droplets could be dispensed on chip into the channel for both devices with 3 um gaskets.
Reservoirs containing buffer solutions of 1 ug/ul luciferase and 400 ug/ml luciferin with 0.1 uM ATP were dispensed as droplets on both 33 um and 21 um electrode EWD devices.

operation_evidence.source_quote: one 18 pl droplet could be dispensed from the reservoir at 17.1 Vrms (1 kHz) with 200 nm Ta2O5 and 200 nm parylene C
The 12 pl droplet was split into two 6 pl droplets at 18.7 Vrms, as shown in the series pictures in Fig. 7.

operation_evidence.bs_operation: bead_droplet = dispense 12 units of ParamagneticBeadSolution / bead_split = split bead_droplet into 2
operation_evidence.source_quote: A 12 pl bead droplet was dispensed on a 33 um electrode device, as shown in Fig. 9. ... The reservoir electrode and the third channel electrode were then turned on to split the bead droplet in (7) and (8).

operation_evidence.bs_operation: reaction = mix bead_split[1] with enzyme / reaction2 = mix reaction with substrate
operation_evidence.source_quote: Both substrate and enzyme solutions could be successfully dispensed and merged on all these devices (Video 2) with the same concentrations used for 100 pl droplet reactions

operation_evidence.bs_operation: light_signal = detect chemiluminescence on reaction2 for 30s
operation_evidence.source_quote: an EMCCD camera (QuantEM, Photometrics), whose working temperature is -30C and quantum efficiency at 560 nm wavelength is 92%, was also tested as a sensor of the chemiluminescent signal, but no light could be detected with such small droplet volumes.

numeric_mismatches.field: water_droplet = dispense 18 units / bead_droplet = dispense 12 units
numeric_mismatches.note: Integer unit counts are used as a direct 1:1 mapping of the paper's stated picoliter volumes (18 pl, 12 pl); BioScript's dispense grammar requires integer literals, so this is a unit-scale approximation rather than an exact picoliter reproduction.

Discarding one split half is a simplification of the paper's specific reservoir-electrode-plus-third-channel-electrode splitting sequence (Figs. 6-9); BioScript's generic 'split into N' primitive does not capture the described electrode-activation sequence or timing.

Temperature and duration for the ATP-luciferin reaction step are not stated explicitly in this paper; a short room-temperature-scale incubation is assumed for modeling purposes, not a value taken verbatim from the text.

numeric_mismatches.field: light_signal = detect chemiluminescence on reaction2 for 30s
numeric_mismatches.note: The paper reports this signal was below the detection limit of both the cooled CCD and EMCCD cameras at picoliter droplet volumes ('no light could be detected with such small droplet volumes'); the detect step models the intended measurement in the assay design, not a signal actually obtained.
